acceptance_criteria: No plaintext secrets in manifests/logs

tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-22. Audit: two stores exist — the live GitHub OAuth vault (AES-256-GCM envelopes in D1, AAD-bound to the user, migration 0012 purges legacy plaintext, lazy re-seal on read) and a 923-line generic user-secrets store that is NOT wired (/api/vault/* answers 503 and nothing imports it). acceptance_criteria: Tenant-mismatched runs refused
Unknown tenants 404
tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-22. Route-level isolation was already covered (403 + workflow.access_denied audit, 404 unknown/unowned, 503 outages, room-ownership fallback, denied trigger records no run). The real hole was on the stamp side: the guard resolved the tenant as 'D1 column first, then the P0.4 room claim', but the trigger handler stamped dag.UserID straight from D1, so a legacy row (workflow_dags.user_id NULL) authorized via the room fallback recorded a NULL tenant — and the runtime's mismatch check is skipped when either side is empty, making the second layer of defence vacuous for exactly those runs. Fix: workflowGuard records the tenant it authorized (workflowOwnerLocals) and the trigger stamps that value, falling back to dag.UserID only when the guard is not installed. Pinned by TestWorkflowTriggerStampsAuthorizedTenantForLegacyDag (NULL-owner DAG claimed by room owner A: A triggers -> 200 and the run carries user-a; B -> 403 and no new row) and TestWorkflowTriggerDeniedInvokesNoRuntime (a refused trigger starts no Cloudflare instance). Resulting invariant: with the boundary on every run that reaches the runtime carries a non-empty tenant, and a mismatch fails the run with NonRetryableError before any step executes.

acceptance_criteria: Cross-site WebSocket hijacking blocked by an Origin allow-list
Ticket is short-lived and single-use

tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-22. W2 (Origin): wsOriginGuard runs before the session guard and refuses a foreign Origin with 403 — middleware rather than an upgrader option because the Fiber websocket config only does exact Origins matching while the allow-list ships an https://*. wildcard; no Origin is allowed (SDK/CLI/e2e, and a browser cannot omit it). W3 (ticket): the URL no longer carries the session token. POST /api/ws-ticket mints a 32-byte random ticket bound to (user, room) with a 15s TTL (engine.WSTicketTTL, the lifetime the SDK already documents); redemption deletes it (GETDEL in Redis, so it is single-use across instances); replay, cross-room use, or a session token in the URL all answer 401, and the ?token= alias was removed. buildWebSocketURL mints a ticket, the SPA fetches one per connect (getWsTicket), and the SDK contract {ticket, expiresIn, expiresAt} is now implemented. Tests: 22 WS cases in backend/pkg/api/ws_auth_test.go (single-use, room binding, TTL, Origin allow-list incl. suffix trick, endpoint 200/403/401) + e2e P05 fetching the ticket over HTTP and upgrading 101. Postman contract + collection + README §7 updated for the new route.

acceptance_criteria: Agent lifecycle states documented
Manifest identity rules fixed
tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-22 (contract + ADR, no runtime consumer). Defined three distinct identities (definition = publisher+name, version = exact semver, instance = tenant deployment) with kind/name as the uniqueness key; name immutable once published; publisher transfer = new publisher; exact pins only. Lifecycle: six states (draft, published, active, paused, retired, obsolete) held in the data layer with an audited transition record, never in the manifest (envelope forbids status; IR invariant I2). Retirement is a tombstone: resolvable for read/audit and existing pins, closed to new pins and new runs, explicit successor, and explicit finish-vs-cancel (retired finishes, obsolete cancels). No registry or deployment store exists yet, so enforcement is DESIGNED.

acceptance_criteria: Provider interface documented
Fake plus Cloudflare impls pass conformance
tasks.description: Contract DONE 2026-11-22 (P7-RUN-001a, DESIGNED): nine operations (start/status/cancel/pause/resume/step/sleep/history/capabilities), step as the only durability primitive, at-least-once delivery with mandatory idempotency keys, six run states plus a separate 'rejected' for admission refusals, capability advertisement that refuses instead of silently downgrading, fixed error taxonomy, and the durable-state vs best-effort-events split (metering reads durable results only). Grounded in the live interpreter which is officially PARTIAL: no cancel, no pause/resume, no declared capabilities(), no unified error taxonomy. P7-RUN-001b DONE 2026-11-23 (adapter + suite): backend/pkg/execution implements the contract types (State incl. rejected, six-class error taxonomy with Classify defaulting unknown errors to permanent, Capabilities with Missing(), ValidatePlan/Admit enforcing tenant + unique names + dependency existence + cycle detection + capability refusal before any step, orderedSteps giving every provider one dependency order). The reference Fake provider is deterministic and synchronous with a durable step log, a separate best-effort event log, retry budgets, step timeouts, crash injection before the durable write, recovery, cancel/pause/resume at safe boundaries and error queues; the conformance suite (C1-C18) runs against a Harness seam and passes 18/18, while a provider advertising nothing runs 14 and reports the 4 capability-gated skips with reasons. The Cloudflare adapter maps the nine operations onto the documented Workflows instance endpoints (create/status/terminate/pause/resume), refuses Sleep and History because sleeps are declared inside the workflow and step events live in D1 logs, advertises exactly cancel+pause, and maps HTTP 401/403 to policy-denied, 429/5xx to transient, everything else to permanent; admission runs locally so a refused plan never reaches the API. acceptance_criteria: UCP spec version pinned
No compliance claimed without tests
tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-22 (research only, no code). Verified against the official repos: UCP (Apache-2.0) uses DATE-BASED protocol versions (spec error example: '2026-01-12 is not supported, this business supports 2026-01-11 and 2026-01-23'), separates protocol-version selection from capability negotiation, serves a profile at /.well-known/ucp, names capabilities reverse-domain (dev.ucp.shopping.checkout) with a schema URL bound to the namespace authority (provenance, not trust), and binds REST + MCP + a JSON-RPC 2.0 Embedded Protocol (A2A as an integration path). AP2 is v0.2 and explicitly a security feature INSIDE a commerce protocol (catalog/checkout APIs out of scope): five roles (Shopping Agent, Credential Provider, Merchant, Merchant Payment Processor, non-agentic Trusted Surface), Checkout + Payment Mandates with receipts as SD-JWT, Human Present vs Not Present flows, hash-chain dispute evidence. Recorded adapter boundary, the 'must not claim' list, five ordered gates, and O22/O23. No compliance claimed.

tasks.title: Skill Loader: agentskills.io SKILL.md onto the shared Gate
tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-23 for all four acceptance criteria, as a pure loader (D8-compatible: no runner, no route, no agent caller). backend/pkg/agentskills parses and validates SKILL.md frontmatter (name 1-64 lowercase slug with folder agreement, description 1-1024, SPDX-shaped license <=80, compatibility/metadata passthrough, allowed-tools), preserves unknown keys in Extensions instead of dropping them, and keeps only mcp/<server>/<tool>@x.y.z entries as pinned refs while bare upstream tool names stay advisory-only (never authority) and a malformed mcp/ entry is rejected instead of silently downgraded. Progressive loading is structural: Card() is name+description with an estimated token cost and a ResolveTokenBudget=100 check, Activate() is the only way to get the body and refuses anything over BodyTokenBudget=5000, and references//assets/ load on demand through Resource() with single-path-element validation plus a filepath.Rel containment check. Trust is caller-supplied (marketplace decision, never a document field): Community scripts are refused until a Verified review, Private/Verified can read them. Bind(grants, now) is a pure intersection against the tenant's live grants (revoked and expired dropped, exact version required) so a skill can only narrow authority; the Gate remains the only execution path, proven by a grantless call that refuses before the transport is touched. Package is backend/pkg/agentskills, not backend/pkg/skills (that name is the existing role-prompt registry) and not backend/pkg/agent/tools (those are LLM tools). NOT done by design: no SSE/persistent sessions, no skill activation in an agent run, no manifest-schema cross-check at load (the docs gate covers the Skill manifest; the loader parses the upstream SKILL.md), and P7-SCH-001 still owns ranking/bounds over these cards.

tasks.title: OpenAPI Importer: one operation maps to one Tool Manifest
tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-23 for all four acceptance criteria, as a loader (no runner, no route, no agent caller). backend/pkg/openapiimport reads OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 JSON or YAML (YAML is converted to JSON so one struct serves both), and Import maps one allowed operation to one pinned Tool Manifest: identity from operationId (slugified) or a stable method+path slug, permissions derived as resource:action, sideEffect/approvals from the method (GET safe, POST/PUT/PATCH external+external-write, DELETE irreversible+human-review), idempotency key from the addressed path parameter (or an explicit idempotencyKey body field for POST), input schema from path/query/non-credential headers with object bodies inlined, output schema from the first 2xx JSON response, tenant required with a configurable contextKey, and provenance from owner/commit. Credentials never reach a manifest: security schemes (apiKey/http/oauth2/openIdConnect/mutualTLS) and credential-shaped headers/cookies (Authorization, X-Api-Key, Cookie, ...) become vault:<publisher>/<slug> references and are removed from the input schema, and an undefined or unsupported scheme is an error instead of a silently unauthenticated tool. The audited surface is mandatory: no allow-list means refusal (AllowAll is the explicit reviewed escape hatch), a typo'd entry fails loudly, deprecated operations are refused, and two operations that collapse to one tool name are an error. Determinism is contractual: output is sorted and canonically serialized (sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline) so bytes are stable, and Merge makes a repeat import idempotent while refusing same-ref/different-content (bump the version instead). Every manifest self-validates against the Tool Manifest contract and maps onto mcp.ToolPolicy, so an ungranted call is denied before any HTTP. NOT done by design: no HTTP transport (the Gate owns execution), no registry persistence, no Code Mode. Package lives in backend/pkg/openapiimport rather than sdk/ because the Gate and the policy vocabulary it maps onto are Go.

tasks.title: Dynamic tool search (search_tools) beside static manifests
tasks.description: DONE 2026-11-23 for all four acceptance criteria, as search beside the gate (no execution, no agent wiring). backend/pkg/toolsearch builds a Catalog from the loaders' own output: AddImported indexes the OpenAPI importer's manifests (pinned ref + description + sideEffect) and AddSkill indexes an agentskills skill's allowed-tools, so search covers exactly what already has a manifest and nothing else. Search(query, limit) ranks with fixed documented weights (name word/substring beats description word/substring, with a phrase bonus), drops one-character and stop-word tokens so common words cannot flatten the ranking, normalises - and _ in names, and breaks ties by score then name then pinned ref, so the same catalog and query always give the same order (golden-tested). Bounds are structural: limit is clamped to MaxCandidates=8, the slice is dropped when it would exceed ContextTokenBudget=600 estimated tokens, and Truncated plus a note say so; the default answer is DefaultLimit=5. A miss is information: the result is empty with Missed=true and a note telling the model to state the missing capability, never a return-everything fallback. Authority stays with the gate: Verify/GrantID resolve a live non-revoked non-expired grant for the tenant, CallRequest refuses an ungranted match with mcp.DeniedError instead of building a request that can only fail, and a test drives a surfaced tool through a real mcp.Gate (no grant = zero transport calls, foreign grant refused, live grant executes once). Code Mode is a gated spike, not a runtime: NewCodeMode needs both an explicit enabled flag and a Sandbox, the zero value and nil receiver refuse, Program/empty input refuse, and a static test asserts the package links no os/exec, plugin or syscall execution facility — so no code path runs agent-authored code unsandboxed. NOT done by design: no server.json/event-log ranking source yet, no real WASM/container Sandbox (sequenced with P7-RUN), no agent or route caller (D8).
